subject.title: [Feature]: Add realtime video frame transport for provider and gateway relay sessions

question: Should OpenClaw add a provider/Gateway realtime video-frame transport now, and what consent, validation, payload, logging, provider-retention, and plugin SDK semantics should that public contract enforce?
rationale: Automation can prove the transport is missing, but deciding whether camera frames may transit Gateway/provider/plugin boundaries creates a product, security, and public API contract that needs maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve narrow one-shot frame transport
options.body: Define an additive single-frame contract with explicit consent assumptions, MIME and size validation, no payload logging, provider-specific mapping rules, docs, and tests before implementation.

options.title: Defer behind browser-direct proof
options.body: Wait for the browser-direct describe_view work at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/89127 to land or be rejected before promoting a broader Gateway relay transport.

options.title: Keep frames out of Gateway
options.body: Reject Gateway relay image transport for now and keep visual context limited to browser-direct or plugin-owned paths that do not require new core protocol surface.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow one-shot frame transport
recommendation.body: Define an additive single-frame contract with explicit consent assumptions, MIME and size validation, no payload logging, provider-specific mapping rules, docs, and tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the current assignee and current-source owner signal for the Talk/Gateway/protocol surfaces that would define this contract.
